   <title>Animation Test</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/animate.css/4.1.1/animate.min.css"/>
    <style>
        .subtitle {
            font-size: 4vw;
            font-weight: normal;
            color: white;
            animation: fadeInUp; 
            animation-duration: 7s; 
        }

        #animation-container {
            position: relative;
            width: 100%;
            background: linear-gradient(to right, #1d3557, #ff8c42);  /* Tropical Punch */
            flex-direction: column; 
            height: 120vh; 
            margin-top: -90px; 
            background-size: cover; 
            background-position: center; 
            background-repeat: no-repeat; 
            overflow: hidden; 
            overflow: clip;  
            contain: content; 
            display: flex; 
            align-items: center; 
            justify-content: center; 
        }

        #canvas {
            position: absolute;
            top: 0;
            left: 0;
            width: 100%;
            height: 100%;
            z-index: 0;
        }

        #animation-text {
            position: absolute;
            z-index: 1;
            top: 50%;
            left: 50%;
            transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
            font-size: 8vw;
            font-weight: bold;
            color: white;
            animation: fadeIn; /* referring directly to the animation's @keyframe declaration */
            animation-duration: 5s; /* don't forget to set a duration! */
        }

}

.image-grid {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 32px;
    justify-content: center;
    align-items: center;
    margin-top: 28px;
}

.image-grid img {
    filter: brightness(0) invert(1);
    opacity: 0;
    max-height: 44px;
    width: auto;
    object-fit: contain;
    transition: opacity 0.35s ease, transform 0.35s ease, filter 0.35s ease;
    animation: logo-rise 0.7s ease forwards;
}

.image-grid img:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: 0.5s; }
.image-grid img:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.75s; }
.image-grid img:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 1.0s; }

.image-grid img:hover {
    opacity: 1 !important;
    transform: translateY(-4px) scale(1.08);
    filter: brightness(0) invert(1) drop-shadow(0 0 10px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.65));
}

@keyframes logo-rise {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(12px); }
    to   { opacity: 0.72; transform: translateY(0); }
}

@media screen and (max-width: 600px) {
    .image-grid {
        gap: 24px;
    }
    .image-grid img {
        max-height: 32px;
    }
}

    <h2 class="title">
      The issue
    </h2>
    <p class="text-right" style="font-size: 10em;"">
      If you ever taught a course on data science, you likely found yourself in this situation: You want to cover the ethics of data science. But have only one or two sessions to do so. And: students have no background in ethics! In short, <mark class="mark-red">how do you teach ethics to non-ethicists</mark> within a session or two — and, perhaps, without having much of a background in ethics teaching yourself?
      You face a similar issue when you want to teach a course on the ethics of data science: You need to cover the basics of data science, but you have at most two sessions to do so, and your students (and perhaps you yourself) have little no background in data science. In short, you need to <mark class="mark-blue">teach data science to non-data scientists.</mark>
    </p>

  <div class="content-box-left">
    <h2 class="title">
      Ethics &#x2715; Data Science
    </h2>
    <p class="text-left" style="font-size: 10em;">
      Ethics &#x2715; Data Science offers resources and materials to teach data science to non-data scientists and ethics to non-ethicists. We prepare and collect tutorials, teaching ideas, and cases to cover some of the basics of data science and ethics. <!-- We aim to capture the latest and best research on the topics, and present it in small modules that could be the basis for individual classroom sessions or self-study. -->

      Our own background is in professional schools of public policy and public administration, where courses have few prerequisites and students expect to learn a lot in a relatively short amount of time. This project has been generously supported by <a href="https://apsia.org/">APSIA</a>, the Association of Professional Schools of International Affairs, the <a href="https://www.hertie-school.org/en/">Hertie School Berlin</a>, and the <a href="https://www.maxwell.syr.edu/">Maxwell School at Syracuse University</a>.
    </p>
